=== usage
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
recover-project: usage: recover-project.sh <name> [target path]

=== no registry
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
recover-project: <TMP>/hub/nowhere not found: first make sure agent-hub itself is cloned

=== not in the registry
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
recover-project: 'nosuch' is not in the project registry (<TMP>/hub/projects): check the spelling, or the project was never registered

=== native project
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
recover-project: 'alpha' was a native project (no external GitHub remote).
So its code was never backed up anywhere but the original machine: the registry entry only has
memory_bare_repo (hubbox:~/git-origin/alpha-memory.git), which is the history of memory tracking, not code.
If the original machine's disk is still there, rescue the code from it first, then decide by hand how to attach
hubbox:~/git-origin/alpha-memory.git; this script will not guess at code.

=== target exists
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
recover-project: <TMP>/home/workspace/kappa already exists, not overwriting: sort it out by hand, then run again

=== recovered
exit 0
--- stdout
[1/5] Preconditions OK: kappa (origin=<TMP>/remotes/o/kappa.git, restoring to <TMP>/home/restore/kappa)
[2/5] Cloned the code from <TMP>/remotes/o/kappa.git
[3/5] .agent-memory is on the existing agent-memory branch of <TMP>/home/git-origin/kappa-memory.git (full history, not a new branch)
sync-local-setup (stand-in): kappa
[4-5/5] Local setup is aligned (rules-file block / hooks / ignores)

Done: kappa is restored to <TMP>/home/restore/kappa, with the full agent-memory history.
--- stderr
